metadata.title: Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks sink as investors flee AI trade

content.text:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock retreated another 5% on Wednesday, following a 6% decline in the prior session as chip stocks continued to plunge amid a broader market sell-off.
Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also extended declines from the prior session.
This year's once-hot AI trades continue to tumble, with memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and peer SK Hynix (SKHY) dropping 6%. Micron is 50% off its all-time high over the summer. Storage and memory players Seagate (STX), Western Digital (WDC), and Sandisk (SNDK) all fell on Wednesday. Sandisk, which recently implemented a stock split, is roughly 70% off its June record high.
The violent move follows a stunning rally on Monday when Nvidia jumped 31% after the AI chip giant's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. But some strategists say tighter financial conditions and lingering questions around the AI trade are weighing on sentiment.
"There is still a lot of nervousness out there, and some investors have taken advantage of Monday's jump to cut their exposure to the AI trade," said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, on Wednesday.
He also said the prevailing view that Huang is the only person who can hold the AI trade together "reeks of desperation," while investors increasingly perceive that "Nvidia's board is not the one that the world's leading chip designer should want."
Other areas of the AI trade retreated, including the stocks of neocloud providers CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS).
